chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the four winds: the north, the south, the east wind, and the west wind. And I said to him: People say that the north wind is from Paradise and the south wind is from the Fire.

So he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has hosts from among the wind by which He punishes those who disobey Him. Over each wind among them is an appointed, obeyed angel. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to punish a people with a punishment, Allah reveals to the angel appointed over that kind of wind which He intends to punish them with, and the angel commands it, so it surges as an enraged lion surges. And each wind among them has a name. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune."
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
"Then a whirlwind containing fire struck it, and it was burned."

And what He mentioned in the Book of the winds by which He punishes those who disobey Him. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has winds of mercy: fertilizing winds, winds that stir the clouds and drive the clouds, winds that hold the clouds between the heaven and the earth, winds that press them so they rain by the permission of Allah, and winds that disperse the clouds, and winds among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has enumerated in the Book. As for the four winds, they are the names of the angels: al-Shamāl, al-Janūb, al-Ṣabā, and al-Dabūr. Over each wind among them is an angel appointed over it. So when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills to make a north wind blow, He commands the angel whose name is al-Shamāl, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strikes with his two wings, then the north wind disperses wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills on land and sea. And when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills to send al-Ṣabā, He commands the angel whose name is al-Ṣabā, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strikes with his two wings, then the wind of al-Ṣabā disperses wherever Allah, Exalted, wills on land and sea. And when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills to send a south wind, He commands the angel whose name is al-Janūb, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strikes with his two wings, then the south wind disperses wherever Allah wills on land and sea. And when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills to send a west wind, He commands the angel whose name is al-Dabūr, and he descends upon the Sacred House and stands at the Yemeni Corner and strikes with his two wings, then the west wind disperses wherever Allah, Exalted, wills on land and sea.

key_terms.الرُّكْنِ الْيَمَانِيِّ: the Yemeni Corner of the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ: the barren wind, a destructive wind mentioned in the Qur’an
key_terms.الرِّيَاحِ: the winds, as divine forces used for mercy or punishment
key_terms.الصَّبَا: al-Ṣabā, one of the four named winds and the name of an angel in this narration
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ الْحَرَامِ: the Sacred House, from which the angel descends in the narration’s description
key_terms.جُنُودًا: hosts or armies under Allah’s command
key_terms.رِيَاحُ رَحْمَةٍ: winds of mercy that benefit creation
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel appointed over each wind

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say about the four winds and their angels?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the winds are among Allah’s forces, used both for punishment and mercy, each under the command of appointed angels. It also connects the phenomenon of winds to Qur’anic descriptions and presents the four named winds as names of angels tasked with directing them by Allah’s command.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1522 - Ali ibn Ri'ab reported from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (as) about the four winds—the North wind (Shamal), the South wind (Janub), the East wind (Saba), and the West wind (Dabur). I told him, "The people say that the North wind is from Paradise and the South wind is from Hell."

Imam (as) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has armies from among the winds with which He punishes those who disobey Him. Each wind has an angel in charge who is obeyed.
When Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, wishes to punish a people with a particular type of wind, He reveals to the angel in charge of that wind that He intends to use it as a punishment. The angel commands it, and it rages as an enraged lion would. Each wind has a name.
Do you not hear the words of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic:
'Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous calamity' (Quran 54:19)
'a whirlwind containing fire, which burned it' (Quran 2:266)?

And what Allah (swt) mentioned in the Book about the winds by which He punishes those who disobey Him.
Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, also has winds of mercy—pollinating winds, winds that stir the clouds and drive them, winds that hold the clouds between the sky and the earth, winds that squeeze the clouds and make them rain by Allah’s (swt) permission, and winds that disperse the clouds.
These are among the winds that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned in the Book. As for the four winds, they are the names of angels—North (Shamal), South (Janub), East (Saba), and West (Dabur). Each of these winds has an angel in charge of it.
When Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, wants to send a north wind, He commands the angel named Shamal, who descends upon the Sacred House (Kaaba), stands by the Yemeni Corner, and strikes with his wings, causing the north wind to scatter wherever Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, wills, over land and sea.
Similarly, when Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, wishes to send the east wind, He commands the angel named Saba, who descends upon the Sacred House, stands by the Yemeni Corner, and strikes with his wings, causing the east wind to scatter wherever Allah (swt) wills over land and sea.
When Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, desires to send the south wind, He commands the angel named Janub, who descends upon the Sacred House, stands by the Yemeni Corner, and strikes with his wings, causing the south wind to scatter wherever Allah (swt) wills.
When Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, intends to send the west wind, He commands the angel named Dabur, who descends upon the Sacred House, stands by the Yemeni Corner, and strikes with his wings, causing the west wind to scatter wherever Allah (swt) wills over land and sea."
